claims.explanation: Repaglinide is a meglitinide insulin secretagogue that closes ATP-sensitive potassium (KATP) channels by binding the SUR1/KCNJ11 complex, and its selective anticancer effect likely reflects dependence of certain tumor cells on KATP channel activity or on the ABCC8/KCNJ11/PPARG pathway for survival. The pattern is not explained by a single common driver mutation; instead, sensitivity appears enriched in lines with PTEN loss/PI3K-AKT pathway activation and in ARID1A-mutant or KMT2C/EP300-mutant chromatin-remodeling contexts, while RAS/BRAF-mutant lines with intact PTEN or with NF1/RB1 loss tend to be less affected. The virtual-cell response (E2F2 up, PCNA down, HMGCS1 down) suggests cell-cycle and metabolic stress rather than a lineage-specific effect.

features.basis: PTEN loss is common in many selectively killed lines (H4, U118MG, SNU81, FTC133, DMS273) and may increase dependence on KATP/PI3K-linked survival signaling
ARID1A mutations appear in multiple sensitive lines (OVTOKO, SW1088, MHHNB11, EFE184, 22RV1) and may create chromatin-remodeling vulnerability
KCNJ11 encodes the Kir6.2 pore of the KATP channel targeted by repaglinide; higher expression could increase drug response
ABCC8 encodes SUR1, the repaglinide-binding subunit of the KATP channel; expression is required for the annotated mechanism
PPARG is an annotated repaglinide target and may mediate metabolic or differentiation effects in responsive lines
KMT2C mutations are enriched in sensitive lines (SNU81, T3M4, 22RV1, FTC133, HT115) and may impair chromatin-based survival programs
EP300 mutations appear in several sensitive lines (SNU81, T3M4, LU99, 22RV1) but also in resistant lines, so this is weaker evidence
TP53 mutation is nearly ubiquitous and not discriminating; some TP53-mutant lines are resistant, suggesting it is not sufficient for sensitivity
KRAS mutations are common in both sensitive and resistant lines, but several resistant lines (CL11, NCIH441, TCCPAN2, GP2D, SNU410) carry KRAS mutations
BRAF mutations appear in resistant lines (HEC265, RL952, OV90) as well as sensitive ones, suggesting MAPK activation may reduce repaglinide sensitivity
NF1 loss occurs in resistant lines (GP2D, SNU410, MDAMB175VII) and may activate RAS-MAPK survival signaling
RB1 mutations appear in resistant lines (SKNAS, OV7) and may reflect cell-cycle deregulation that limits repaglinide response
